source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check CPLD could be flash and update
1. Boot into OS.
2. Use tool to flash last CPLD version file.
3. Reboot and boot into OS.
4. Check the CPLD version.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure CPLD could be flash successfully.2. Check the CLPD version is correct after update

deepseek_columns.ai_packages_needed: CPLD flash tool + latest CPLD image (user-provided)
deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Update: flash and update the CPLD to the latest version. Agent can read the current CPLD version sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "cat /sys/devices/platform/*/cpld_ver 2>&1; dmesg 2>&1 | grep -i cpld | tail -n 10 2>&1" ; the actual flash uses the vendor CPLD tool + image and is a firmware write.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the pre-flash CPLD version + the post-flash version after reboot so the user confirms the CPLD flashed successfully and the version is correct.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: CPLD flash updates on-board CPLD logic; use the approved image and never auto-run mid-system.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; correctly treats flashing as a firmware write but provides only a wildcard version read and no executable validated update/recovery plan.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds exact CPLD identity, signed image/hash, compatibility, stable power, reboot and recovery gates.
historical_reviews.round_02: PARTIAL; separates version read from write but treats package/approval as a capability limit.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms no wildcard or unbounded latest image is safe and post-version must be mapped.

original_test_intent: Flash the exact approved target firmware to the identified onboard CPLD, reboot the platform as required, verify the target CPLD version and confirm that boot, power/reset/control and management health remain normal.
original_method: Capture current CPLD identity/version, validate the target image/hash and vendor tool/recovery, execute one approved flash with full transcript, perform one controlled reboot, then query the same mapped CPLD for target version and collect platform health evidence.
manual_activity: An authorized user supplies and approves the CPLD/image/tool/recovery manifest and later issues the verdict. No inherent physical setup or observation is required when the supported vendor updater and electronic recovery/console path are available; the flash/reboot/readback sequence can be automated.
required_inputs: Exact board/CPLD device/revision and current version
Approved exact target version/image/hash/signature/release notes—not 'last' or 'latest'
Vendor flash tool/version/exact command/prompts and referenced script content/version
Compatibility, backup/rollback or recovery programming procedure
Stable power, maintenance window, active-workload check, reboot/reconnect timeout and OOB/KVM recovery
safety_requirements: Do not flash a wildcard-selected CPLD or unbounded latest/last image; positively bind image to the target.
Do not use /sys/devices/platform/*/cpld_ver without mapping the matched node to the intended CPLD.
Preserve baseline and full flash failure output, maintain stable power and stop on any identity/hash/transfer/verify mismatch.
Do not auto-retry, power-cycle blindly or continue after boot/OOB loss; use only the approved recovery path.
agent_execution_scope: Validate target/image/tool/script/recovery identities and capture mapped current version plus BIOS/BMC/SEL/kernel health.
After one-user approval, run the exact vendor flash transaction once with complete output and then issue one controlled reboot/reconnect sequence.
Query the same CPLD for target version, verify platform control/boot/management health and report raw Tool Result without setting PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the exact CPLD target, image/hash, vendor tool and recovery plan.
Approve maintenance/reboot boundaries and remain available for hardware recovery.
Review flash/version/health evidence and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The read-only version/log probe is useful only after mapping the sysfs node; the wildcard can select the wrong device. It does not supply the vendor flash command, target version or recovery and cannot prove update success.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use only the owner/vendor-validated CPLD updater and exact signed image, then run a mapped version query and health checks after one controlled reboot.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: OS-based flash, one reboot, post-version check, referenced script URL and 10/10-minute fields are preserved; 'last' is converted to an explicit approved target only at project readiness.

modernized_recommendation.status: EXISTING VENDOR METHOD WITH VERSION PINNING
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed CPLD update manifest and automation that captures target/current version, image/tool hashes, full flash/verify output, reboot milestones, mapped post-version and control-plane health.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact board/CPLD/update path in the approved manifest.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record board/CPLD/BIOS/BMC, updater, script and image versions/hashes.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Approved vendor CPLD update/recovery documentation and referenced internal cpld_update script; script content was not available in the repository.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Pins 'last' to an exact target and makes recovery and evidence atomic without changing the flash method.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; flash success, correct version and platform recovery are all required.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: CPLD firmware can control power, reset, thermal or mux logic; a successful process exit does not establish functional health.

project_override_considerations: A project may approve an exact target/tool/reboot plan. Missing artifacts are readiness gates, not PARTIAL. A different target or recovery profile applies only to that plan and must be reported explicitly.
expected_evidence: Board/CPLD current-target manifest, signed image/hash, tool/script versions and authorization
Pre-version plus BIOS/BMC/SEL/kernel/control-state baseline and stable-power/recovery proof
Complete flash/verify transcript and controlled reboot/downtime/reconnect timeline
Mapped exact target version, boot/power/reset/thermal/management health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently require a CPLD update and correct post-update version. 'Last' is ambiguous target selection but a project readiness input, not contradictory source semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target operation and acceptance are clear. Image/tool/recovery availability is readiness; with a supported electronic updater and OOB path, the full core is automatable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains firmware risk and readback support but rejects wildcard evidence and PARTIAL based on package supply.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains exact identity/image/recovery gates while advancing capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under the V3.1 package/approval rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Binds pre/post evidence to the same CPLD and adds control-plane health beyond a version string.

review_improvement: Prevents wrong-device or unbounded-target flashing, preserves failures and correctly distinguishes high-risk readiness from automation capability.
independent_technical_reasoning: The source describes an OS/vendor-tool firmware transaction, reboot and electronic version check. After exact artifacts and approval, none of these core steps inherently require manual physical action, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is correct.

no_automatic_retry: One validated flash and one approved reboot only. Preserve any failure and invoke the approved recovery path under engineer control; never repeat or switch images automatically.
